sentences.text: Nagesh Katam ..... Petitioner

Mr. R.L. Pattnaik, Advocate
 Vs.
State of Orissa .....

Opposite Party
 Mr. D.K. Mishra, Aga
 Coram:
 Justice Savitri Ratho
 Order

15.11.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
01.
1.

This application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed in connection with Orkel P.S. Case No.
211 of 2023 corresponding to G.R. No. 241 of 2023 in the court of the learned J.M.F.C.,
Kudumuluguma where chargesheet has been filed against the petitioner for commission of offence punishable under Section 376 (2) (n) of the IPC read with Section 67 (A) of IT Act.
2.
This is the second journey of the petitioner to this Court praying for bail.
The earlier application i.e. BLAPL No. 10748 of 2023 had been disposed of granting liberty to the petitioner to move the learned trial court for bail afresh after 2 weeks.
3. The prayer for bail of the petitioner having been rejected vide 02.11.2023 passed in B.A. No. 213 of 2023 by the learned Sessions Judge, Malakangiri, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. The prosecution allegations in brief against the petitioner are that the petitioner had kept physical relationship with the victim giving her the assurance of marriage.
5. Perusal of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. reveals that she has stated that she was in love with the petitioner since 3 years.
The petitioner had obtained her mobile number and they spoke for about 8 months over telephone now and then he comes to her house to visit her.

In 2021 November, they professed their love for each other and thereafter after 8 months,
the petitioner had taken the victim on his motor cycle to his house and she stayed there for two days and they had physical relations there on one or two occasions.

1 knowledge he has videographed their act and also captured her nude photographs in his mobile.
Although he had assured to marry her, he has sent her pictures to her brother and other friends.
In the year, 2022, he committed sexual assault on her without her will and consent.
6. Mr. R.L. Pattnaik, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 05.07.2023 and investigation has been completed.
As it is a case of consent, the prayer for bail of the petitioner should be sympathetically considered.

He further submits that though the I.O. has seized his mobile, but report from the RFSL, Berhampur has not been received for which the allegations regarding circulation of the nude photographs of the victim on social media is not made out against the petitioner.
He further submits that as the chargesheet does not disclose that the I.O. has seized any photographs of the victim stated to have been circulated by the petitioner.

7. Mr. D.K. Mishra, learned Additional Government Advocate opposes the prayer for bail stating that the victim has stated that initially the petitioner had physical relationship with the victim without her consent and thereafter though they have had physical relations on few occasions on the assurance of marriage, he has clicked her nude photographs and video without her knowledge and has circulated the photographs by sending them to her brother and other friends and Debendra Padiami, brother of the victim has confirmed the said allegation in his statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
He further submits that the charge has been framed in the case for which if the petitioner released on bail, he is likely to tamper with the evidence.

8. Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner and as charge has been framed in the meantime, I am not inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
9.
The BLAPL is accordingly dismissed.
10. The petitioner is at liberty to renew his prayer for bail before the learned court below after examination of the victim girl.
11. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
(SAVITRI RATHO) JUDGE puspa Signed by: PUSPANJALI MOHAPATRA
